newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.KOREA MULLS AID TO KOREA FIRST BANK.
newsitem.headline: S.KOREA MULLS AID TO KOREA FIRST BANK.

text.p: South Korea's Finance Ministry has been considering various ways to help Korea First Bank which has been hit by a chain of loan defaults by big conglomerates, the chief ministry spokesman said on Wednesday.
"We are considering some government supports to help improve the financial status of Korea First Bank," spokesman Chung Eui-dong told reporters.
He said the government was concerned about a move by Standard and Poor's Corp to downgrade the credit rating of Korea First Bank, which might prevent the bank from issuing long-term bonds.

The bank's long-term debt is currently rated BBB-minus by S&P, down from BBB-plus in April. If the rating agency were to downgrade Korea First Bank by another notch, the bank would immediately become speculative grade.
Chung said the government measures included special loans from the central bank, rights issue offerings or lower provisions for non-performing loans.
Korea First Bank had already asked for three trillion won in special loans from the central bank.
The bank had been hurt badly after Hanbo Steel collapsed in January with 5 trillion won in debts and Sammi Steel fell in March under debts of more than 1.45 trillion won.
It faced its third major blow in less than a year as the Kia Group, which has piled up 9.5 trillion won in debts, was put under bankruptcy protection last month by its creditors.
Seoul media said the government was considering allowing Korea First Bank to raise its capital by offering a rights issue which the government would plan to undertake.
Another measure under consideration was lowering the bank's won reserve requirement from the current 90 percent of bad loans, the media said.
But Chung declined to elaborate on what was being considered.
